column1: # Command table — the single source of truth for the `devcontainer` command
# surface. `show_usage` in dev/devcontainer and all three shell completions
# emitted by dev/devcontainer-completions are GENERATED from this file; the
# only other place a command appears is the dispatch in dev/devcontainer,
# and tests/test-completions-sync.sh guards dispatch <-> table equality.
# Adding a subcommand: add the dispatch arm in dev/devcontainer, add a row
# here. That is the whole workflow — usage text, the bash/zsh/fish word
# lists, their descriptions, and the argument wiring all follow.
# Tab-separated, seven columns; `#` comments and blank lines are ignored.
#   name        subcommand as typed; must equal a dispatch arm.
#   arg-syntax  what `show_usage` prints after the name (e.g. `[--yes]`,
#               `<file>|-`); `-` for a command that takes no argument.
#   arg-type    argument completion class, one of:
#   arg-label   human label for the argument: zsh's `_values` group name for
#               arg-words, and fish's `-d` text for a file/dir argument.
#   short-desc  one-line description shown in zsh/fish completion menus.
#   usage-desc  the longer `show_usage` prose. Use a literal `\n` to force a
#               line break; the generator indents continuations under the
#               description column. Keep lines under ~80 columns after the
# The generator rejects a malformed table (duplicate name, unknown arg-type,
# empty description, wrong column count, `:` inside an arg-word description,
# leading/trailing whitespace in any column) rather than emitting a broken
# completion script. CRLF line endings are tolerated: the `\r` is stripped.
